parsed.rationale: The TLV loop bounds checks use ICHECK(i, 2+len) against bodylen, but the actual packet buffer is only guaranteed by ND_TCHECK2(*message, 2+len) which checks the captured length. However, several cases read fields beyond the checked len (e.g., MESSAGE_ACK_REQ reads message+6 with len<6 check but ND_TCHECK2 only covers 2+len; MESSAGE_UPDATE reads message+12 with len-10 and network_prefix; MESSAGE_MH_REQUEST reads message+16 with len-14). More critically, the loop condition i < bodylen does not ensure cp+4+i+2+len stays within the captured packet; ND_TCHECK2(*message, 2+len) does check that, but the ICHECK macro compares against bodylen not the actual captured length, and bodylen is attacker-controlled from the packet. Also MESSAGE_HMAC loop reads message[4+j] for j<len-2, i.e., up to message[2+len], which is within the ND_TCHECK2(*message, 2+len) range but the check is 2+len bytes starting at message, so message[2+len] is the last valid byte—OK. The main concern is that bodylen is not validated against the actual captured length, so the loop can iterate over TLVs beyond the packet; ND_TCHECK2 catches reads but the ICHECK(i, 2+len) uses bodylen as the bound, allowing len to be large and i+2+len to exceed bodylen only checked via ICHECK. This is a known CVE area (babel dissector) with potential out-of-bounds reads.
